## Basic Usage

State persists across cells:

````markdown
```{term}
export GREETING="Hello from quarto-term"
```

```{term}
echo $GREETING
```
````

```{term}
export GREETING="Hello from quarto-term"
```

```{term}
echo $GREETING
```

## Multi-Line Commands

Loops and other multi-line constructs work automatically via PS2 detection:

````markdown
```{term}
for i in 1 2 3; do
  echo "Item $i"
done
```
````

```{term}
for i in 1 2 3; do
  echo "Item $i"
done
```

## ANSI Colors

Colored output renders faithfully:

````markdown
```{term}
printf '\033[31mred\033[0m \033[32mgreen\033[0m \033[34mblue\033[0m\n'
```
````

```{term}
printf '\033[31mred\033[0m \033[32mgreen\033[0m \033[34mblue\033[0m\n'
```

## Working with Files

````markdown
```{term}
echo "line 1" > /tmp/demo.txt
echo "line 2" >> /tmp/demo.txt
echo "line 3" >> /tmp/demo.txt
cat /tmp/demo.txt
```
````

```{term}
echo "line 1" > /tmp/demo.txt
echo "line 2" >> /tmp/demo.txt
echo "line 3" >> /tmp/demo.txt
cat /tmp/demo.txt
```

## Piping

Multi-line pipes work naturally:

````markdown
```{term}
seq 1 5 |
paste -sd+ |
bc
```
````

```{term}
seq 1 5 |
paste -sd+ |
bc
```

## Line Options

Line options let you control how each line is delivered to the shell. Append them using the marker (default `#!`). See the [Reference](reference.qmd#line-options) for the full list of line options.

### Interrupting a Command

Send a long-running command, then interrupt it with Ctrl-C:

````markdown
```{term}
sleep 100 #! expect-prompt: false
ctrl-c #! literal: false, delay: 0.5, expect-prompt: true
```
````

```{term}
sleep 100 #! expect-prompt: false
ctrl-c #! literal: false, delay: 0.5, expect-prompt: true
```

The first line sets `expect-prompt: false` because `sleep` won't produce a prompt. The second sends Ctrl-C (`literal: false` interprets it as a key name), waits 0.5s, and then expects the prompt to return.

### Arrow Key Navigation

Recall and re-execute the previous command using multiple space-separated keys on one line:

````markdown
```{term}
echo "first command"
up enter #! literal: false, delay: 0.3
```
````

```{term}
echo "first command"
up enter #! literal: false, delay: 0.3
```

When `literal: false`, space-separated words are sent as individual keys. Only the last key triggers `hold` and `expect-prompt`. See [Special Keys](reference.qmd#special-keys) for all recognized key names.

### Cell-Level Defaults

Set `literal: false` and `delay` as cell defaults to avoid repeating line options. Individual lines can still override with explicit `#!` options:

````markdown
```{term}
#| literal: false
#| delay: 0.2
echo "first command" #! literal: true
up
enter
```
````

```{term}
#| literal: false
#| delay: 0.2
echo "first command" #! literal: true
up
enter
```

### Per-Line Timeout

Use a longer timeout for a specific slow command without changing the document default:

````markdown
```{term}
echo "fast"
sleep 2 && echo "slow" #! timeout: 5.0
echo "back to normal"
```
````

```{term}
echo "fast"
sleep 2 && echo "slow" #! timeout: 5.0
echo "back to normal"
```

```{term}
#| include: false
rm -f /tmp/demo.txt
```
